body.p: In the Non-Final Office Action,l the Examiner took the following actions:

1. rejected claim(s) 1-2, 8-9, and 14-15 under 35 U.S.C. 103 as being unpatentable over LI, Xiao-fei (CN 112819790 B, "LI"), in view of UMEMATSU, Terumi (WO 2018179150 Al, "UMEMATSU"), and further in view of D'MELLO YANNICK (CA 3181091, "D'MELLO"); and

2. objected to claims 2-7, 10-13, and 16-20 as being dependent upon a rejected base claim, but would be allowable if rewritten in independent form including all of the limitations of the base claim and any intervening claims. By this Amendment, Applicant has amended claims 1, 8, and 14. The amendments are fully supported by the original disclosure. See, e.g., Applicant's application, [0024] and [0048]. Upon entry of this Amendment, claims 1-20 are pending and under examination.
Applicant respectfully requests reconsideration and withdrawal of the rejections, and the timely allowance of the pending claims for at least the reasons set forth below.

Applicant respectfully traverses the rejection of claim(s) 1-2, 8-9, and 14-15 under 35 U.S.C. 103 as being unpatentable over LI, in view of UMEMATSU, and further in view of D'MELLO. A primafacie case of obviousness has not been established.

"The key to supporting any rejection under 35 U.S.C. 103 is the clear articulation of the reason(s) why the claimed invention would have been obvious.... [R]ejections on obviousness cannot be sustained with mere conclusory statements." M.P.E.P. § 2142, 9th Ed. Rev. 08.2017 (Jan. 2018) (internal citation and inner quotation omitted). "[T]he framework for the objective analysis for determining obviousness under 35 U.S.C. 103 is stated in Graham v. John Deere Co., 383 U.S. 1, 148 USPQ 459 (1966). ... The factual inquiries .. .are as follows: (A)

1 The Non-Final Office Action may contain a number of statements reflecting characterization of the related art and the claims. Regardless of whether any such statement is identified herein, Applicant declines to automatically subscribe to any statement or characterization in the Non-Final Office Action.

[d]etermining the scope and content of the prior art; and (B) [a]scertaining the differences between the claimed invention and the prior art; and (C) [r]esolving the level of ordinary skill in the pertinent art." M.P.E.P. § 2141(II). In rejecting a claim, "Office personnel must explain why the difference(s) between the prior art and the claimed invention would have been obvious to one of ordinary skill in the art." M.P.E.P. § 2141(III).

Independent claim 1, as amended, recites "processing the facial video to obtain a plurality of quasi-heart rates and a plurality of quasi-vibration frequencies of eyes or mouth of the target object, wherein the quasi-heart is obtained through one or more of a region of interest (ROI) between eyebrows and an ROI of chin, and the quasi-vibration frequency is obtained through one or more of an ROI of the eyes and an ROI of the mouth," (emphases added). The cited references, whether taken alone or in any combination, fail to disclose or suggest at least these elements.

In the rejection of claim 1, the Examiner mapped "color difference signal" to "a plurality of quasi-vibration frequencies" recited in claim 1. Applicant respectfully submits that: 1) the term "color difference signal" is shown nowhere in the Abstract of LI cited by the Examiner; and 2) the Examiner did not articulate how "a plurality of quasi-vibration frequencies" is mapped to the "color difference signal". Further, the Examiner alleged that the plurality of quasi-vibration frequencies is for estimating the heart rate value of the target tracking object. Applicant respectfully submits that the plurality of quasi-vibration frequencies recited in claim 1 is a plurality of quasi-vibration frequencies of eyes or mouth of the target object, which is not used to estimate a heart rate value of the target object (emphasis added). To further clarify, Applicant amended claim 1 to recite "a plurality of quasi-vibration frequencies of eyes or mouth of the target object," (emphasis added).

For at least the reasons discussed above, LI does not disclose or suggest "processing the facial video to obtain a plurality of quasi-heart rates and a plurality of quasi-vibration frequencies of eyes or mouth of the target object, wherein the quasi-heart is obtained through one or more of a region of interest (ROI) between eyebrows and an ROI of chin, and the quasi-vibration frequency is obtained through one or more of an ROI of the eyes and an ROI of the mouth," as recited in amended claim 1 (emphases added).
The Examiner also asserted that UMEMATSU and D'MELLO each discloses certain

element(s) of claim 1. Without acquiescing to the Examiner's assertions, Applicant respectfully submits that UMEMATSU and D'MELLO, whether taken alone or in any combination, also fail to disclose or suggest the above-quoted elements of amended claim 1, and thus do not cure the deficiencies of LI.

In view of the above, the Office has neither properly determined the scope and content of the cited references nor properly ascertained the differences between the claimed invention and the cited references. Moreover, the Office has articulated no reason as to why one of ordinary skill in the art would find the claimed combination obvious in view of the references, despite these differences. For at least this reason, no prima facie case of obviousness has been established with respect to claim 1. Claim 1 is thus allowable.
Amended independent claims 8 and 14, although different in scope from independent

claim 1, recite elements similar to those of claim 1 discussed above. Thus, for reasons similar to those discussed above, claims 8 and 14 are allowable. Claims 2, 9, and 15 are also allowable at least by virtue of their dependence from claim 1, 8, or 14.
Accordingly, Applicant respectfully requests withdrawal of the rejections of claim(s) 1-2, 8-9, and 14-15 under 35 U.S.C. 103.

Applicant acknowledges with appreciation the identification of claims 2-7, 10-13, and 16-20 as allowable if rewritten in independent form including all of the limitations of the base claim and any intervening claims.

In view of the foregoing amendments and remarks, Applicant respectfully requests Examiner's favorable consideration and timely allowance of all pending claims.
